newsitem.title: POLAND: Early zloty slips lower vs basket, support holds.
newsitem.headline: Early zloty slips lower vs basket, support holds.

text.p: The Polish zloty eased against the basket in early Monday trade as some took profits on last week's zloty rise, but the local unit remained a safe distance from central bank-guarded support levels at -1.5 pecent.
The zloty slipped to -1.31/-1.39 percent from parity at 0830 GMT from from opening's -0.76/-0.86 mainly as a result of domestic bank currency-buying, dealers said.

"The market continues to be volatile and today's zloty fall was mainly caused by domestic bank speculation," said Piotr Czyzewski, dealer at ING bank in Warsaw. "But the morning mood may change and the zloty could return to around -1.0 percent."
The zloty was at 3.4665/85 to the dollar, down from opening's 3.4430/60 and at 1.8790/10 to the mark, against 1.8720/40. The U.S. unit traded around 1.8440 per mark.

The zloty was battered down to record lows against its currency basket two-weeks ago before slowly making up lost ground last week on the back of central bank (NBP) currency-selling and speculative capital inflows.

However, analysts said the zloty's outlook remained bearish as Poland's current account deficit expanded quickly despite a monetary policy tightening in 1997, which the NBP said would be continued in future months to cap booming domestic demand.

At Monday's 1.1 billion zloty T-bill tender yields are expected to rise, but demand should be capped by better secondary market offerings, which were up to 50 bp higher than comparable maturities at primary offers, dealers said.
The money market remained swamped with cash in the last days of the monthly reserve period and one-day rates tumbled as banks wanted to place cash at nearly all costs, dealers said.

Overnight rates slipped one point from opening to 2.00/6.00 percent and tomorrow/next were at 4.36/13.00 percent against Friday's close at 20.00/22.20 percent. The monthly reserve period ends on July 30. -- Wojciech Moskwa +48 22 653 9700
